name: CommandPalette
usage: Global search and jump (`Mod+K`), running actions by name, finding people and files

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called when the palette asks to open or close (`Esc`, clicking outside, running an item).

props.name: items
props.description: The items, matched locally while typing (see matchCommands).

props.name: onSearch
props.description:
Searches more items for a query, such as people or files on a server. Called 150 ms after typing stops; the
signal is aborted when the query changes or the palette closes. The results are shown after the local
matches, as they are (not matched again).

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder of the search field, "Search or run a command" by default (follows `locale`).

props.name: emptyText
props.description: Text shown when nothing matches, "No results" by default (follows `locale`).

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the dialog and the search field, "Command palette" by default (follows `locale`).

props.name: limit
props.description: Largest number of results shown; beyond it, a line below the list says how many more there are.

types.name: CommandPaletteItem
types.summary: An item of a CommandPalette: a page to go to or an action to run.

fields.name: group
fields.description: Group shown at the end of the row, such as "Pages" or "Actions"; items of a group are kept together.

fields.name: icon
fields.description: Icon at the start of the row: a name, or an icon component such as Lucide's `Settings`.

fields.name: keywords
fields.description: Extra words that also match, such as synonyms or an English name.

fields.name: shortcut
fields.description: Shortcut hint shown with Kbd, such as `'mod+n'`.

fields.name: onSelect
fields.description: Runs the item; the palette closes first.

types.name: IconName
types.summary:
Name of a registered icon. Only the icons listed here can be used; they are Lucide icons under shorter names
(`trash` is Lucide's `Trash2`, `more` is `Ellipsis`). All names at runtime: `iconNames`. Props that take an
icon also accept an icon component instead of a name (see IconComponent).

types.name: IconComponent
types.summary:
An icon component, such as Lucide's `Plus` (`import { Plus } from 'lucide-react'`), accepted wherever an icon name
is: `<Button icon={Plus}>`, `<Icon icon={Plus} />`, menu items and so on. Names (`icon="plus"`) are convenient
and work in data such as menu configurations, but cover only the registered icons (`iconNames`); a component can
be any Lucide icon, or an SVG of your own. Both are drawn with the same size, stroke width and `tone`.

types.name: IconComponentProps
types.summary:
Props that Icon passes to an icon component. Lucide icons (`import { Plus } from 'lucide-react'`) accept them; a
component of another icon set, or an SVG of your own, works too if it accepts them, or passes them on to its
`<svg>`.

fields.name: strokeWidth
fields.description:
Stroke width in the units of a 24 × 24 view box, already scaled for `size`: the line is 1.75 px wide on screen
by default, whatever the size.

fields.name: color
fields.description:
Stroke color: `currentColor` (the text color) or a semantic color variable, such as
`var(--vl-color-danger)`.

fields.name: aria-hidden
fields.description: `true` for a decorative icon (hidden from screen readers).

fields.name: aria-label
fields.description: Accessible name of a meaningful icon.

examples.name: Basic
examples.title: Basic usage
examples.description:
Open it with the button or `Mod+K` (registered with useHotkeys), type to filter, `↑` / `↓` and `Enter` to run.
Matching is fuzzy: "nwp" finds "New project". HotkeysProvider keeps the `Mod+K` of this example from clashing
with the one of the page that shows it.

examples.name: ManyResults
examples.title: Many results
examples.description: At most `limit` results (50 by default) are shown; a line below the list says how many more there are.

examples.name: AsyncSearch
examples.title: Searching a server
examples.description:
`onSearch` adds results from a server after the local matches. It is called when typing stops, and the
signal is aborted when the query changes; "Searching" appears only when the search takes a while.
